answer: Anchor each agent to one DNS domain it controls. First, it publishes a DNSSEC-signed TXT record holding its public key, so the domain becomes its passport. Second, the registry accepts only domains at least 90 days old, verified at the registrar, blocking bulk sign-ups. Third, each year the agent renews and re-signs a fresh challenge, or lapses. Forging 10,000 fakes costs 10,000 aged domains, $120,000, 90 days waiting, plus 10,000 checks. Like a marble slab stamped at its quarry, a walnut off one tree, or a reef built one polyp at a time, identity is slow and singular, not mass-produced.
